question:
There are three different products that need to be processed on three machine tools. Each product must be processed first on machine 1, then sequentially on machine 2 and 3. The order of processing the three products should remain the same on each machine. Assume \( t_{ij} \) represents the time it takes to process the \( i \)th product on the \( j \)th machine.

**Given:**

- \( t_{11} = 5 \) minutes, \( t_{12} = 4 \) minutes, \( t_{13} = 3 \) minutes
- \( t_{21} = 6 \) minutes, \( t_{22} = 5 \) minutes, \( t_{23} = 4 \) minutes
- \( t_{31} = 7 \) minutes, \( t_{32} = 6 \) minutes, \( t_{33} = 5 \) minutes

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every numeric constant from the problem lives here.
# t[i][j] = processing time (minutes) of product i on machine j, 1-indexed
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DATA = {
    "t": (
        (None, 5, 4, 3),   # product 1: machines 1,2,3
        (None, 6, 5, 4),   # product 2
        (None, 7, 6, 5),   # product 3
    ),
    "n_products": 3,
    "n_machines": 3,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["n_products"]
    m = d["n_machines"]
    t = d["t"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ----- Sets ------------------------------------------------------------
    model.P = pyo.RangeSet(1, n)   # products (jobs), in fixed processing order
    model.M = pyo.RangeSet(1, m)   # machines, in fixed routing order
    model.Mr = pyo.RangeSet(1, m - 1)  # machines except the last
    model.Pr = pyo.RangeSet(1, n - 1)  # products except the last

    # ----- Variables -------------------------------------------------------
    # C[i, j] : completion time of product i on machine j
    model.C = pyo.Var(model.P, model.M, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ----- Objective -------------------------------------------------------
    # Minimise makespan = completion time of the last job on the last machine
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.C[n, m], sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ----- Constraints -----------------------------------------------------

    # (a) Routing / precedence within each product:
    #     product i must finish on machine j before it starts on machine j+1.
    #     C[i, j+1] >= C[i, j] + t[i][j+1]      (>= because it is a *must finish first*)
    def routing_rule(model, i, j):
        return model.C[i, j + 1] >= model.C[i, j] + t[i][j + 1]

    model.routing = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.Mr, rule=routing_rule)

    # (b) Machine capacity in the fixed product order:
    #     on machine j, product i+1 can only start after product i is finished.
    #     C[i+1, j] >= C[i, j] + t[i+1][j]      (>= because of no-overlap)
    def machine_rule(model, i, j):
        return model.C[i + 1, j] >= model.C[i, j] + t[i + 1][j]

    model.machine_seq = pyo.Constraint(model.Pr, model.M, rule=machine_rule)

    return model

"""
======================================================================
Permutation Flow Shop Scheduling - 3 products x 3 machines
----------------------------------------------------------------
Decision variables:
  C[p, m]  in Reals (>= 0)   completion time of product p on machine m
                             p = 1..3 (products), m = 1..3 (machines)
  Cmax     in Reals (>= 0)   makespan = completion time of last product
                             on last machine

Objective (in words):
  MINIMISE the makespan Cmax, i.e. the total time for all three products
  to flow through the three machines in the fixed (permutation) order.

Constraints (numbered, with source sentence):
  (1) First product on first machine: C[1,1] >= t[1,1]
      "Each product must be processed first on machine 1"
  (2) First product on later machines: C[1,m] >= C[1,m-1] + t[1,m]
      "then sequentially on machine 2 and 3"
  (3) Later products on first machine: C[p,1] >= C[p-1,1] + t[p,1]
      "The order of processing the three products should remain the same
       on each machine" (machine 1)
  (4) Later products on later machines:
      C[p,m] >= C[p-1,m] + t[p,m]   (same machine, previous product)
      C[p,m] >= C[p,m-1] + t[p,m]   (same product, previous machine)
      "The order of processing the three products should remain the same
       on each machine" + sequential machine processing
  (5) Makespan: Cmax >= C[p,3] for all p
      "minimise the total processing time"
======================================================================
"""

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    n = d["num_products"]
    m = d["num_machines"]
    t = d["t"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Index sets
    model.P = pyo.RangeSet(1, n)   # products
    model.M = pyo.RangeSet(1, m)   # machines

    # Decision variables
    model.C = pyo.Var(model.P, model.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # (1) First product, first machine
    def rule_c11(mdl):
        return mdl.C[1, 1] >= t[(1, 1)]
    model.con_first_product_first_machine = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_c11)

    # (2) First product, later machines (sequential on machines)
    def rule_first_product(mdl, j):
        if j == 1:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return mdl.C[1, j] >= mdl.C[1, j - 1] + t[(1, j)]
    model.con_first_product_seq = pyo.Constraint(model.M, rule=rule_first_product)

    # (3) Later products, first machine (permutation order on machine 1)
    def rule_first_machine(mdl, i):
        if i == 1:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return mdl.C[i, 1] >= mdl.C[i - 1, 1] + t[(i, 1)]
    model.con_first_machine_order = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_first_machine)

    # (4) Later products, later machines
    def rule_general(mdl, i, j):
        if i == 1 or j == 1:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return mdl.C[i, j] >= mdl.C[i - 1, j] + t[(i, j)]
    model.con_same_machine_order = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.M, rule=rule_general)

    def rule_general_seq(mdl, i, j):
        if i == 1 or j == 1:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return mdl.C[i, j] >= mdl.C[i, j - 1] + t[(i, j)]
    model.con_same_product_seq = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.M, rule=rule_general_seq)

    # (5) Makespan definition
    def rule_cmax(mdl, i):
        return mdl.Cmax >= mdl.C[i, m]
    model.con_cmax = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_cmax)

    # Objective
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

DATA = {

    "machines": [1, 2, 3],
    # proc_time[i][j] = time to process product i on machine j
    "proc_time": {

    # upper bound on makespan (sum of all processing times)
    "big_M": 5 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 7 + 6 + 5,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    t = d["proc_time"]
    big_m = d["big_M"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=products, ordered=True)
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=machines, ordered=True)

    # start time of each product on each machine
    model.start = pyo.Var(model.I, model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                          bounds=(0, big_m))

    # makespan
    model.C_max = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, big_m))

    # Objective: minimize makespan
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.C_max, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Precedence within a product: machine j+1 starts after machine j finishes
    def rule_product_precedence(m, i, j):
        if j == machines[-1]:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.start[i, j + 1] >= m.start[i, j] + t[(i, j)]

    model.product_precedence = pyo.Constraint(
        model.I, model.J, rule=rule_product_precedence)

    # No overlap on each machine: fixed product order 1 -> 2 -> 3
    def rule_machine_order(m, i, j):
        if i == products[-1]:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.start[i + 1, j] >= m.start[i, j] + t[(i, j)]

    model.machine_order = pyo.Constraint(
        model.I, model.J, rule=rule_machine_order)

    # Makespan: completion of last machine operation for every product
    def rule_makespan(m, i):
        return m.C_max >= m.start[i, machines[-1]] + t[(i, machines[-1])]

    model.makespan_def = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=rule_makespan)

    return model

    num_machines = d["num_machines"]
    t = d["t"]
    M = d["big_M"]

    model.I = pyo.RangeSet(1, num_products)
    model.J = pyo.RangeSet(1, num_machines)

    # Pairs of distinct products (i < k) for sequencing binaries
    pairs = [
        (i, k)
        for i in range(1, num_products + 1)
        for k in range(i + 1, num_products + 1)
    ]
    model.Pairs = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2)

    # Completion time of product i on machine j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.I, model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Makespan
    model.C = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Sequencing binary: 1 if product i precedes product k
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.Pairs, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize makespan
    def obj_rule(m):
        return m.C

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Precedence within a product's own route: machine j after machine j-1
    def route_rule(m, i, j):
        if j == 1:
            return m.x[i, j] >= t[(i, j)]
        return m.x[i, j] >= m.x[i, j - 1] + t[(i, j)]

    model.route = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.J, rule=route_rule)

    # Machine capacity: for each pair i<k and each machine j, either i before k or k before i
    def seq_rule1(m, i, k, j):
        return m.x[k, j] >= m.x[i, j] + t[(k, j)] - M * (1 - m.y[i, k])

    def seq_rule2(m, i, k, j):
        return m.x[i, j] >= m.x[k, j] + t[(i, j)] - M * m.y[i, k]

    model.seq1 = pyo.Constraint(model.Pairs, model.J, rule=seq_rule1)
    model.seq2 = pyo.Constraint(model.Pairs, model.J, rule=seq_rule2)

    # Makespan definition
    def makespan_rule(m, i):
        return m.C >= m.x[i, num_machines]

    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=makespan_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Processing times t[i][j] (minutes), from the problem statement.
    "t": {
        (1, 1): 5, (1, 2): 4, (1, 3): 3,   # t11=5, t12=4, t13=3
        (2, 1): 6, (2, 2): 5, (2, 3): 4,   # t21=6, t22=5, t23=4
        (3, 1): 7, (3, 2): 6, (3, 3): 5,   # t31=7, t32=6, t33=5
    },
    "products": [1, 2, 3],   # three products, fixed order
    "machines": [1, 2, 3],   # three machine tools, fixed sequence 1->2->3
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    products = d["products"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    t = d["t"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=products, ordered=True)   # products
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=machines, ordered=True)   # machines

    # Start time of product i on machine j
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.I, model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # Makespan
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: minimise makespan
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Precedence within a product: machine j -> machine j+1
    def rule_machine_order(m, i, j):
        if j == machines[-1]:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.s[i, j + 1] >= m.s[i, j] + t[(i, j)]
    model.machine_order = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.J, rule=rule_machine_order)

    # Fixed product order on each machine: product i -> product i+1
    def rule_product_order(m, i, j):
        if i == products[-1]:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.s[i + 1, j] >= m.s[i, j] + t[(i, j)]
    model.product_order = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.J, rule=rule_product_order)

    # Makespan definition: completion on last machine
    def rule_makespan(m, i):
        return m.Cmax >= m.s[i, machines[-1]] + t[(i, machines[-1])]
    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=rule_makespan)

    return model
